raw.query: WITH c AS (SELECT variate,resolution,origin,h,step,ts,y_true,point FROM provenance.v_forecast_thesis_corpus WHERE model='chronos' AND mode='cov'), u AS (SELECT variate,resolution,origin,h,step,ts,y_true,point FROM provenance.v_forecast_thesis_corpus WHERE model='chronos' AND mode='uni'), p AS (SELECT c.variate,c.resolution,abs(c.y_true-c.point) AS cov_ae,abs(u.y_true-u.point) AS uni_ae FROM c JOIN u USING (variate,resolution,origin,h,step,ts) WHERE c.y_true IS NOT DISTINCT FROM u.y_true), v AS (SELECT resolution,variate,100.0*(AVG(cov_ae)/NULLIF(AVG(uni_ae),0)-1) AS pct_change FROM p GROUP BY resolution,variate) SELECT resolution,ROUND(AVG(pct_change)::numeric,6) AS macro_pct_change,ROUND(MIN(pct_change)::numeric,6) AS min_variate_pct,ROUND(MAX(pct_change)::numeric,6) AS max_variate_pct,COUNT(*) AS variates FROM v GROUP BY resolution ORDER BY CASE resolution WHEN '1min' THEN 1 WHEN '45s' THEN 2 WHEN '30s' THEN 3 WHEN '15s' THEN 4 WHEN '1s' THEN 5 END
raw.evidence: Macro-averaging each variate's covariate-versus-univariate MAE change reproduces every claimed value after rounding; all populations are exactly paired with matching truths and current, non-superseded runs.
